definition: The practice of using human judges to assess the quality, helpfulness, safety, or other properties of a model's outputs.
details: Human evaluation remains an important complement to automated metrics, since many desirable qualities of LLM output — such as helpfulness, tone, or nuanced correctness — are difficult to fully capture with automatic benchmarks alone.

explainer.lead: Human judges are used to rate model outputs for qualities automated metrics handle poorly, such as helpfulness, tone, or nuanced correctness. It matters because many of the properties users care about most resist clean automatic scoring.

tiers.eli5: Instead of letting a computer grade the answers, you ask people to read them and say which are good.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run human evaluation alongside automated benchmarks, often with rubric-based ratings or side-by-side preference comparisons. A common pitfall is rater disagreement or inconsistent instructions, so clear rubrics and agreement checks are needed.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the practice of using human judges to assess quality, helpfulness, safety, or other properties of model outputs; it is a complement to automated metrics rather than a replacement, since some desirable qualities are difficult to fully capture automatically.

explainer.example: A team has raters score two model responses to the same prompt for helpfulness and tone, then compares the preference rates to decide which version to ship.
